Subject: Post-call readout: resource squeeze & TCO framing for Finverity

Thanks again for your time this afternoon — quick recap and clear next steps so we stay aligned. Short version up top, details below.

TL;DR
- Primary pain: unpredictable inference spend when traffic spikes (end-of-day batch jobs + user peak minutes) and limited ops headcount to constantly tune models.
- Goal: deliver LLM-powered underwriting assistance inside Finverity’s dashboard at <$0.04 per user session equivalent (target), maintain <120ms median token latency for interactive flows.
- Early levers: batching windows for async scoring, prefix/KV caching for repeated policy templates, and lighter quantized variants for lower-priority batch runs.

What we heard (confirming pain + impact)
1) Resource squeeze at month-end: your team gets a ~4x burst in requests between 20:00–22:00 UTC that trips budget alerts and degrades latency for interactive users.
2) Ops bandwidth is tight: currently each model change requires manual rollout and rollback, so you prefer wider safety margins versus aggressive optimization.
3) Cost target: leadership wants a conservative ceiling on inference op-ex spend for pilot month to evaluate ROI before expanding.

Preliminary TCO picture (high level; attached spreadsheet has numbers)
- Baseline (no batching/caching): est. $22k/month for 1M sessions (median tokens/session ~1,200).
- With conservative batching and KV prefix caching applied to async scoring: est. $9k–12k/month (40–55% savings on token compute).
- Add dedicated reserved capacity and quantized model for non-interactive pipelines: down to $6k–8k/month with predictable latency SLOs.

Key tradeoffs we flagged
- Bigger batching reduces unit cost but increases tail latency for the batched cohort — acceptable for end-of-day scoring, not for interactive assists.
- Prefix caching delivers large savings for your repeated policy templates (you have high cache hit potential), but requires a short integration to map template keys.

Requested next steps (proposed timeline)
1) We’ll send a short TCO worksheet (attached) adjusted for your actual tokens/session distribution — action: Kimberly to deliver by Wed EOD (attached).
2) Technical deep-dive on prefix/KV caching and rollout safety controls — action: Ben to schedule a 45-min session next week with your infra team.
3) Pilot scope proposal: 6-week pilot focused on batch scoring + one interactive assist path, with committed reserved slots for predictable throughput — action: Marissa will draft pilot SOW and propose pricing.

Attachments: finverity-tco-draft-v1.xlsx (draft numbers), call-recording-20260928.mp3

Open questions for you (please confirm in reply)
- Is the 1M sessions/month assumption in the attached worksheet accurate for your pilot window?
- Do you have a strict maximum acceptable tail latency for interactive assists (p95 or p99)?

Thanks again — appreciate the clarity on constraints. If any of the above is off, call it out and we’ll adjust.

—

Kimberly — thanks for the clear summary. Quick confirmations and a couple of clarifications: 

- 1M sessions/month is the right ballpark for pilot (we modeled 900k–1.1M). Good to see the attached numbers.
- Tail latency: for interactive underwriting assist, p95 <= 300ms is what product leadership wants; p99 can be relaxed to 750ms for now.
- Ops constraint: our infra team (Tom) wants a turnkey rollout plan — low-friction steps they can hand off to platform engineers.

Two asks from our side:
1) Could you produce a simple ROI line that shows net cost per approved application assuming model reduces manual review by 18%? We’ll map approvals/month to revenue impact.
2) We have a short security questionnaire relevant to KV caches (where cached content may include masked PII). I’ll drop that in a follow-up email.

If you can update the sheet with p95 requirement and the ROI line, we’ll review and aim to commit to a pilot go/no-go in our Oct 12 leadership sync.

On the demo: Tom and I would like a 30–40 minute walkthrough of the caching flow — Tom is available Wed 6–8pm UTC or Thu morning PST.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Product, Finverity
elena@finverity.com
